title: Corporate Event Planning — Budget Benchmarks & Norms
content:
# Corporate Event Budget Benchmarks
*Last updated: Feb 2026*

## Per-Head Cost Ranges (Full-Day Corporate, 75–150 pax)

| Line Item | Low | Mid | High |
|---|---|---|---|
| Venue (room + basic AV) | $120/head | $200/head | $320/head |
| Catering (breakfast + lunch + breaks) | $85/head | $115/head | $160/head |
| AV/Production (full-day tech) | $35/head | $55/head | $90/head |
| Floral/Décor | $15/head | $22/head | $40/head |
| Photography (half-day) | $18/head | $28/head | $45/head |
| Printed materials + signage | $8/head | $14/head | $22/head |
| Planner fee (flat, corporate tier) | — | $4,500–$6,500 | — |

## Notes
- Boston-area venues trending 8–12% higher YoY in 2026 vs 2025
- Catering inflation running ~6–8% in 2026; get updated quotes early
- AV costs relatively stable; ClearSignal has been reliable and competitive
- Floral vendors: significant variance in 2026 pricing; get 2–3 quotes

## Typical Corporate Event Timeline (from signed contract)
- T-16 weeks: Venue hold confirmed
- T-12 weeks: Vendor contracts signed
- T-8 weeks: Catering menu finalized, dietary confirmed
- T-6 weeks: AV/run-of-show walkthrough
- T-3 weeks: Client delivers branded assets
- T-1 week: Final headcount, printed materials to printer
- Day-of: Rachel on-site from load-in through dinner reception close

title: Corporate RFP Proposal Template — Notes
content:
# Corporate RFP Proposal — Structure Notes

## What returning clients want to see
- One-page executive summary (event vision, date, venue, total investment)
- Itemized budget table with per-head breakdown
- Vendor slate with brief rationale for each selection
- Timeline overview (key milestones from contract to day-of)
- Reference to prior event outcomes (shows continuity and trust)

## Veridian-specific notes
- Marcus shares proposal directly with CFO (Priya Nair) — keep language clean and non-jargony
- Sub-$45K keeps it below CFO sign-off threshold; model to $42–44K to give Marcus room
- Always include a 'what's new this year' section — they like to see evolution, not copy-paste
- Dietary accommodations table is appreciated (they've mentioned it twice)

## Common RFP mistakes to avoid
- Vague vendor descriptions ('a local florist') — name the vendor and their specialty
- Missing contingency line — always include 3–5% buffer
- No cancellation/rescheduling policy summary — corporate clients need this for internal approval

## Pricing strategy
- Rachel's fee for returning corporate clients: $5,000–$5,500 flat (bump from $4,500 given scope growth)
- Frame total investment as 'per-person' in summary — $420–440/head sounds more digestible than $44K total

title: Corporate Event Planning — Budget Benchmarks & Norms
content:
# Corporate Event Budget Benchmarks & Norms

## Overview
Reference benchmarks for corporate events in the 75–150 pax range, NYC/tri-state market. Updated from 2024–2025 actuals and industry contacts.

## Catering (per head, full-day corporate)
- **Floor (basic):** $75–$80/head — continental breakfast, boxed lunch, afternoon break
- **Mid-range (standard):** $85–$95/head — plated or buffet lunch, AM/PM breaks, passed apps at cocktail hour
- **Premium:** $100–$120/head — multi-course plated, premium bar, chef stations
- **2025 Harvest Table actual (Veridian, 100 pax):** $88/head → $8,800 total
- **2026 realistic floor for comparable package:** $90–$92/head → $9,000–$9,200 for 100 pax
- **Note:** Food cost inflation running ~5–7% YoY in NYC catering market as of early 2026. $92/head is a defensible floor; $95 is a safe midpoint estimate.

## AV & Production (full-day, 100 pax, hybrid-capable)
- **Floor (basic in-house):** $2,000–$3,500 — venue-provided AV, no hybrid
- **Mid-range (external vendor, hybrid):** $6,500–$8,500 — dedicated AV company, screens, mics, streaming
- **Premium (full production):** $10,000–$18,000 — LED walls, broadcast-quality streaming, full crew
- **2025 ClearSignal actual (Veridian):** $7,200
- **2026 realistic floor (same scope, returning vendor):** $7,000–$7,200

## Floral & Décor (corporate, 100 pax)
- **Floor (minimal):** $1,800–$2,500 — registration table arrangement, simple centerpieces
- **Mid-range (standard):** $3,500–$4,500 — stage backdrop, 8–10 centerpieces, registration, directional
- **Premium:** $5,500–$8,000 — full floral design, custom installations
- **2025 Bloom & Branch actual (Veridian):** $3,800
- **2026 realistic floor (same scope):** $3,800 — revert to 2025 actuals, skip premium add-ons
- **Note:** Bloom & Branch raised prices ~8% for 2026 on premium tiers; base package pricing held. See [[Florist Alternatives — Corporate Events]] for backup options.

## Venue (full-day, 100 pax, NYC-adjacent conference center)
- **Floor:** $4,500–$6,000 — basic conference room, no add-ons
- **Mid-range:** $6,000–$9,000 — ballroom or large conference space, standard setup
- **Premium:** $10,000+ — luxury hotel ballroom, full-service
- **Meridian Grand Ballroom 2026:** $6,200 (flat from 2025)
- **Foyer add-on 2026:** $1,400 (up from $1,150 in 2025 — 22% increase)

## Contingency
- Standard: 5–8% of event subtotal
- Minimum recommended floor: $1,800–$2,000 for 100-pax corporate event
- Do not compress below $1,800 without client acknowledgment

## Planner Fee (Rachel Summers Events)
- Corporate events: $4,800–$6,500 depending on scope and lead time
- Standard for returning client, full-service: $5,200
- Always structured as separate line item outside client event budget cap

title: Veridian 2026 — Foyer Pivot Decision Log (2026-03-26)

# Veridian 2026 — Foyer Pivot Decision Log
**Date:** 2026-03-26
**Anchor event:** Meridian rate card email received (MSG-5010)

## What Changed
Meridian confirmed foyer add-on at **$1,650** — not $1,400 (modeled in WB-3) and not $1,200 (negotiation target). Rate is firm per venue language. This arrived the morning of 2026-03-26, after the informal budget preview had already been sent to Marcus Chen.

## Execution State at Time of Pivot
- Budget preview sent: YES (TODO-507 complete) — Marcus has seen a figure near $44,950 (trimmed model) or $47,450 (base model); need to confirm exactly what was shared.
- Foyer positioned as: solved registration-flow solution for 100-pax layout
- RFP writing block: EVT-303, days away
- Open quotes: Harvest Table catering + ClearSignal AV — both still pending as of today

## Cross-Reference Check
- [[OBSN-1]] Budget Benchmarks: Foyer/pre-function space typically runs $1,200–$1,800 for 100-pax corporate events in this market. $1,650 is within normal range but above the modeled figure.
- [[OBSN-3]] Venue Research — Meridian: Foyer flagged as 'strongly recommended' for 100-pax registration flow due to main ballroom entry bottleneck. Not flagged as operationally mandatory — note from site visit mentions that a well-staffed single-entry setup with staggered arrival windows can work for groups up to 110 pax. Foyer-free is viable but requires tighter day-of coordination.

## Decision Axes
| Option | Budget Impact | Operational Risk | Client Relationship Risk |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|------------------------|
| A — Drop foyer | -$1,650, lands ~$44,050 | Medium — re-pitch registration layout | Low-Medium — need to re-frame |
| B — Absorb at $1,650, find cuts | Depends on pending quotes | High — two quotes still open | Low if cuts found cleanly |
| C — Reset ceiling with Marcus | +$700 ask | Low | Medium — ceiling was a hard parameter |

## Recommendation (Pre-Call)
Lead with Option A in Marcus call/email — frame as a rate confirmation that opens a layout conversation, not a budget failure. Foyer-free is operationally viable per OBSN-3 site notes. If Marcus pushes back on registration flow, offer Option B contingent on pending quotes landing favorably.

title: Dual-Assurance Pattern — Prevention Protocol
content:
# Dual-Assurance Pattern — Prevention Protocol

Created: 2026-04-26 following Bloom & Branch / Kowalski-Reyes conflict.

## What Happened

Rachel gave a price-hold assurance to client Dana Kowalski (Feb 18) and a rate-cooperation assurance to vendor Sophie Marchetti / Bloom & Branch (Apr 19 phone call). These commitments were incompatible and neither was cross-checked against the other at the time of making.

Root cause: vendor-side assurance made verbally during an informal call, not logged in client file or Notion event record. No conflict check performed before speaking.

## Prevention Rules (effective immediately)

1. **Before making any vendor-side commitment that touches a client budget line**: check the signed contract and client communication log for that event first.
2. **Any verbal assurance to a vendor about pricing or rate flexibility must be logged in Notion within 24 hours** — in both the vendor note AND the relevant event record.
3. **Never use open-ended language like 'work with you on this' with vendors** without a defined scope. If flexibility exists, state the ceiling explicitly or say 'I'll need to review each event individually.'
4. **Dual-role check**: when acting as vendor relationship manager, explicitly ask — 'Does this conflict with anything I've told the client for this event?'

## Affected Weddings — Immediate Action Required

- **Kowalski-Reyes (May 9)**: Conflict active — see NPAG-9 for resolution path.
- **Chen-Okafor (Jun 27)**: Review Bloom & Branch commitment language before any further vendor contact. No client assurance confirmed yet — do not make one until rate situation is resolved.
- **Patel-Williams (Aug 23)**: Same as Chen-Okafor. Sufficient lead time for proactive client disclosure if needed.
